title: I23a track: historical on-chain acquisition and the first per-edge replay on real inputs (human answer Q5)

predictions.claim: Every decoded successful commit's parentBatchHeader hashes (keccak256) to the batchHash of the latest CommitBatch event for that batch index before the transaction; 0 exceptions, reverts and recommits included.
Every real parent header has length 249 or 257, is accepted by the frozen ok_sol and ok_go, and its enc_sol(dec(.)) round trip differs at most in the sequencerSetVerifyHash cells 185..216.
Headers with a nonzero sequencerSetVerifyHash form a prefix of the batch sequence (every one has a lower batch index than every header whose field is zero), and at least one header has it zero.
Only header versions 0 and 1 occur on mainnet in the window; version 2 never appears.

For every batch whose latest commit was a commitBatch carrying blobs, the header's blobVersionedHash (seen in the next commit's parent) equals that transaction's first blob versioned hash; 0 exceptions.
At least 99% of the commit blobs in the window are retrievable (beacon API or blob archive), and every retrieved blob's KZG commitment hashes to its versioned hash.
The real Go decoders of the pinned checkout (common/batch) agree with the frozen dec_go/ok_go on every real parent header.
The window holds the whole history: the earliest committed batch index is 1, the indices cover 1..max without gaps, and every reverted batch is recommitted within the window.
Every successful commit transaction after the proxy's last Upgraded event in the window decodes under the pinned ABI.

regressions.claim: Gates M0, M1 and M2 pass; statements, statuses and gen files of M0, M1 and M2 are unchanged.
Construction: the index of a fixed sub-window is byte-identical across runs; no secret in any output; the snapshot is outside the repo; header_checks passes the toy headers.
